## TINEA UNGUIUM (ONYCHOMYCOSIS)
Obtain a fungal stain of nail sample prior to initiating treatment. Using large
nail clippers, remove as much of the unattached dystrophic nail as possible.
Place the piece of clipped nail plate in formalin jar and send to pathology for
fungal stain (PAS). Treatment should only be initiated if stain is positive for
fungal elements. Fungal culture is NOT recommended.
Systemic therapy is most likely to achieve a cure, especially with more nail
involvement. If <25% involvement topical therapy may be considered. If >50-75%
involvement systemic therapy should be considered.
Toenails take 12-18 months to grow out completely, so improvement should not be
expected to be observed for at least 6-9 months. Continued improvement can be
experienced following treatment completion.
## Oral Treatment:
Terbinafine works about 70% of the time to cure the fungus, and reinfection is
common, so many patients will need to do more than one course of treatment.
Fluconazole pulse dosing response rate is approximately 50%. May consider
retreatment with oral therapy after one year.
Recommend Dermatology Consult for retreatment after failure of 2 courses of
terbinafine or fluconazole.
## Preferred Terbinafine first-line oral:
Toenail infections treat for 12 weeks. Obtain baseline liver enzymes prior to
starting. Repeat LFTs if treating for longer than 6 weeks and there were
baseline abnormalities, pre-existing liver disease, or other risks for
hepatotoxicity.
[Terbinafine 250 mg PO qday for 12 weeks (R,H,DI,O]](psjzid-terbinafine-250mg-po-qday)
Fingernail infections treat for 6 weeks. Obtain baseline liver enzymes prior to
starting. Repeat LFTs if treating for longer than 6 weeks and there were
baseline abnormalities, pre-existing liver disease, or other risks for
hepatotoxicity.
Terbinafine 250 mg PO qday for 6 weeks [R,H,DI,O]
## Alternative oral therapy:
Toenail infections treat for at least 6 months
Fluconazole 300 mg PO q week for total of 6 months [R,DI]
Fingernail infections treat for 3 months
Fluconazole 300 mg PO q week for 3 months [R,DI]
## Topical Treatment:
Ciclopirox is a topical first-line treatment for both fingernails and toenails.
Complete resolution occurs in approximately 7 percent of patients treated daily
for 48 weeks. Ciclopirox is a well-tolerated treatment. Potential side effects
include temporary nail changes and local skin irritation.
Ciclopirox 8% nail lacquer: Apply once daily to affected nail(s)
Remove with rubbing alcohol every 7 days. [M] See accompanying medication
pamphlet for specific instructions. Treatment is continued until nail clearance
or up to 48 weeks.
